bank.question: A 'Permit to Work' is just a suggestion and can be ignored if you are experienced in the task

bank.question: You must wear eye protection whenever there is a risk of flying particles entering your eyes, even for a very quick task
bank.explanation: This is true because eye protection must be worn whenever there is a risk of flying debris, dust, or chemical splashes reaching the eyes

bank.question: Which of the following types of fire should you NEVER use a water extinguisher on?
bank.explanation: Class B fires involve flammable liquids; water will spread the liquid and make the fire worse. Carbon dioxide or powder should be used
options: Wood and paper fires (Class A)
Electrical fires (Class E)
Metal fires (Class D)
Flammable liquid fires, such as petrol or oil (Class B)

bank.question: If you find a slightly damaged power cable on a drill, it is okay to use it as long as you wrap it in electrical tape
bank.explanation: This is false because if a tool is damaged, it must be taken out of use, labeled as faulty, and reported to your supervisor immediately

bank.question: What is commonly known as a 'toolbox talk'?
bank.explanation: A 'toolbox talk' is a short, focused safety briefing delivered to workers on-site regarding specific tasks or risks
options: A formal meeting at the head office to discuss company profits
A short health and safety talk on a specific subject given to the workforce
A training session on how to use manual hand tools safely
A disciplinary meeting regarding a breach of safety rules

bank.question: What is the standard voltage for portable power tools used on UK construction sites to improve safety?
bank.explanation: In the UK, 110-volt tools (usually powered via a yellow transformer) are used to reduce the risk of a fatal electric shock
options: 230 Volts
400 Volts
110 Volts
24 Volts

bank.question: What should you do every time you are about to use your PPE?
bank.explanation: Checking PPE for damage ensures it will still provide the intended level of protection during the shift
options: Check if it is the right colour for the site
Check if it is the most expensive brand
Check that it is clean and not damaged
Ensure it is at least two years old

bank.question: Frequent contact with mineral oils and solvents can lead to a skin condition known as dermatitis
bank.explanation: This is true because skin contact with certain oils and chemicals can cause dermatitis, a painful condition that makes the skin itchy, red, or cracked

bank.question: What does the term 'manual handling' mean in a construction environment?
bank.explanation: Manual handling relates to any activity requiring a person to exert force to lift, lower, push, pull, or carry a load
options: Only when lifting objects above head height
Any activity involving lifting, lowering, pushing, pulling or carrying a load
Only when the weight of the item exceeds 25kg
The use of a forklift or crane to move materials around site

bank.question: Site management should monitor controls rather than assuming they remain effective
bank.explanation: This is true because inspection and supervision confirm whether controls are being used and still work.

bank.question: According to health and safety guidelines, when is it generally acceptable to use a ladder as a workstation?
bank.explanation: Ladders should only be used as a last resort for short-duration work (less than 30 minutes) and where the risk is low
options: Short-duration, light work only
Working at height for the whole day
A primary platform for heavy lifting
When you have forgotten your scaffolding legs

bank.question: Which of these statements is true regarding Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome (HAVS)?
bank.explanation: Hand-arm vibration syndrome (HAVS) is a permanent condition; preventing it through tool maintenance and time limits is essential
options: The symptoms usually disappear after a weekend of rest
It is a permanent condition that cannot be cured
It only affects workers over the age of 50
It can be cured with a short course of medication

bank.question: Why is 110V electricity (yellow plugs and cables) preferred over 230V (blue/red) on construction sites?
bank.explanation: The use of 110V (yellow) equipment reduces the risk of a fatal electric shock compared to standard 230V domestic supply
options: 110V equipment reduces the risk of a fatal electric shock
110V cables are thicker and therefore much harder to trip over
Standard 230V plugs do not fit into the sockets on a building site
Tools run faster and with more power when using 110V electricity

bank.question: At what point should Respiratory Protective Equipment (RPE) be used to control dust?
bank.explanation: RPE must be the last line of defence. If a task can be done without creating dust or by using water suppression, those methods must be used first
options: After all other ways to control the dust have been considered first
Only when the weather is very dry and windy
Only if the worker feels like wearing it that day
Every time you enter the site, regardless of the task

bank.question: Whose legal responsibility is it to provide you with basic Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)?
bank.explanation: Employers have a legal duty to provide required PPE for free; employees must use it correctly and report any loss or damage
options: Provide it free of charge
Tell you where to buy it
Deduct the cost from your wages
Only provide it if you have an accident

bank.question: What should you look for on a power tool to ensure it has been checked for electrical safety?
bank.explanation: Checking for a valid PAT (Portable Appliance Testing) sticker is the standard way to ensure an electrical tool is safe to use on site
options: The manufacturer's logo
A valid PAT (Portable Appliance Testing) sticker or tag
A CE mark on the plastic casing
The name of the previous person who used it

bank.question: What can happen if you use high-vibration power tools for long periods of time?
bank.explanation: Vibration from tools can cause permanent damage to nerves and blood vessels; frequent breaks help reduce the cumulative impact
options: Numbness or tingling in the fingers (Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome)
Improved blood circulation and grip strength in the hands
Building up a tolerance so you can work longer shifts
The tool becoming more efficient over time

bank.question: What does the acronym 'HSE' stand for in the context of UK health and safety?
bank.explanation: HSE stands for the Health and Safety Executive, the body responsible for enforcing health and safety law in the UK
options: High Safety Energy
Health and Security Environment
Health and Safety Executive
Hazard and Safety Entry

bank.question: You must always wash your hands before eating or smoking, even if you have been wearing gloves
bank.explanation: This is true because washing your hands before eating or smoking prevents you from ingesting harmful substances or bacteria like Weil's disease

bank.question: Welfare facilities should include suitable washing, drinking water and toilet arrangements
bank.explanation: This is true because adequate welfare is part of basic site health, safety and dignity requirements.

bank.question: What is the main precaution to take when working near overhead power lines?
bank.explanation: Overhead power lines are extremely dangerous; you must maintain a safe distance and follow specific clearance guidance
options: Check if the lines are insulated
Touch them with a wooden pole to see if they are live
Stay well away and follow the site's 'clearance' rules
Work as normal if the weather is dry

bank.question: Why must you attend a site induction before starting work?
bank.explanation: A health and safety induction explains the specific hazards, evacuation routes, and site rules for that particular project
options: To sign your contract of employment
To pick up your wages for the week
To learn about the specific rules and hazards of that site
To meet all the other workers on the site

bank.question: Who has a legal duty to take care of the health and safety of 'themselves and others' on site?
bank.explanation: Health and safety laws require everyone on a construction site to look out for their own safety and the safety of others who might be affected by their actions
options: Only the Site Manager
Only the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) inspector
Only those who have been on site for over a year
Everyone on the site regardless of their role

bank.question: What does a blue circular sign with a white symbol represent?
bank.explanation: A blue circular sign indicates a 'Mandatory' action, meaning you must follow the instruction shown
options: A hazard or danger is nearby
You must carry out a specific action (Mandatory)
An action is strictly prohibited
Information about site exits and first aid

bank.question: Falls from height are the most common cause of fatal accidents in the construction industry
bank.explanation: This is true because hSE statistics show that falls from height remain the single biggest cause of workplace fatalities in the UK construction industry

bank.question: Which type of fire extinguisher should NEVER be used on an electrical fire?
bank.explanation: Fire extinguishers are categorised by the type of fire they can put out; using a water extinguisher on an electrical fire can lead to electrocution
options: CO2 (Carbon Dioxide) or Powder
Water or Foam
None-water extinguishers are safe for electrical fires
Wet Chemical only

bank.question: Providing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is the most effective way to control a hazard on a construction site
bank.explanation: This is false because pPE is a last resort; hazards should first be removed or controlled at the source through engineering or design

bank.question: Which government body is responsible for enforcing health and safety law on construction sites?
bank.explanation: The Health and Safety Executive (HSE) is the national independent regulator for health and safety in the UK
options: The Local Council Construction Office
The Health and Safety Executive (HSE)
The Site Manager's Association
The National Building Insurance Board

bank.question: Which of the following is true about Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome (HAVS)?
bank.explanation: White-finger or Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome (HAVS) is a serious industrial disease that can cause permanent damage to nerves and blood vessels
options: It is a temporary condition that goes away after a rest
It is a permanent condition that cannot be cured
It is a minor skin irritation caused by chemicals
It is another name for a broken finger

bank.question: What does a circular blue sign with a white symbol mean?
bank.explanation: Blue round signs are 'Mandatory' signs, meaning you MUST follow the instruction shown on the sign
options: A warning of danger
Information about a fire exit
A mandatory instruction (must do)
A prohibition (must not do)

bank.question: Occupational health risks may take years to show symptoms
bank.explanation: This is true because exposures such as noise, dust and vibration can cause long-term harm that is not immediately obvious.

bank.question: What is the recommended voltage for portable power tools used on a UK construction site?
bank.explanation: Any electrical equipment used on a construction site should be 110 volts (often marked by a yellow plug) to reduce the risk of a fatal electric shock
options: 230 Volts (standard domestic)
400 Volts (industrial)
110 Volts (yellow plug/transformer)
Battery power only is allowed on site

bank.question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) often referred to as 'the last resort'?
bank.explanation: PPE is considered the last line of defence because it only protects the wearer and does not remove the hazard itself
options: It is the last line of defence if other controls fail
It is always the most expensive option
It is the most effective way to remove a hazard
It is only required by law for supervisors

bank.question: Emergency assembly points should be known and kept clear
bank.explanation: This is true because workers need a safe, identifiable place to gather during evacuation.

bank.question: COSHH assessments are only required for chemicals that have a 'toxic' skull and crossbones symbol on the packaging
bank.explanation: This is false because cOSHH assessments are required for any substance that could be hazardous to health, including common items like cement, wood dust, and paints

bank.question: Why is it dangerous to get wet cement on your skin or inside your boots?
bank.explanation: Skin contact with wet cement can cause severe chemical burns and dermatitis
options: It causes immediate frostbite to the skin
It is harmless as long as it dries quickly
It can cause serious chemical burns and skin problems
It is only dangerous if you swallow it

bank.question: Employees have a legal responsibility to cooperate with their employer on health and safety matters
bank.explanation: This is true because under the Health and Safety at Work Act, you must cooperate with your employer to enable them to meet their legal duties

bank.question: An employer is allowed to charge a worker for the basic PPE they need to do their job safely
bank.explanation: This is false because the employer is responsible for providing all necessary PPE at no cost to the employee

bank.question: It is acceptable to put hazardous waste into a general waste skip as long as it is at the bottom
bank.explanation: This is false because hazardous waste, such as oily rags or chemicals, must be disposed of in specific containers and never mixed with general site rubbish

bank.question: What is the meaning of a circular sign with a red border and a red cross-bar over a black symbol?
bank.explanation: A circular sign with a red border and a diagonal cross-bar indicates that a specific action or entry is prohibited
options: A prohibition sign (Do not do)
A mandatory sign (Must do)
A safe condition sign
A directional sign

bank.question: What is the main purpose of a site induction?
bank.explanation: The main purpose of a site induction is to explain the specific safety rules and hazards of that particular site to keep everyone safe
options: To find out where the nearest pub is
To sign your contract of employment
To be told about site-specific hazards and safety rules
To be given your own personal set of site drawings

bank.question: According to the Work at Height Regulations, what is a key requirement for any work above ground?
bank.explanation: Before working at height, the law requires that the work is properly planned and that edge protection, like guardrails, is in place to prevent falls
options: A soft landing system must be on the ground below
You must be wearing a full-body harness regardless of the task
The work must be properly planned and edge protection provided
There must be at least three people present at all times

bank.question: Working at height only means work above two metres
bank.explanation: This is false because work at height includes any place where a person could fall a distance liable to cause personal injury.

bank.question: Under which regulations must serious work-related accidents be reported to the authorities?
bank.explanation: The Health and Safety Executive (HSE) must be notified of certain serious accidents, diseases, and dangerous occurrences under RIDDOR
options: RIDDOR
COSHH
LOLER
CDM

bank.question: Overhead power lines can be dangerous even without direct contact
bank.explanation: This is true because electricity can arc across gaps, especially where plant or materials get too close.

bank.question: You notice the outer casing of a power tool is cracked and wires are visible. What should you do?
bank.explanation: If tools or machinery are faulty, they must be taken out of use and reported immediately to prevent injury
options: Try to fix it yourself with electrical tape
Continue using it until the shift ends
Use it only for light work tasks
Stop using it, unplug it, and report it to your supervisor

bank.question: Fire doors may be wedged open when the site is busy
bank.explanation: This is false because fire doors are designed to restrict the spread of smoke and flame and should not be wedged open.

bank.question: Health and safety laws only apply to full-time employees and do not cover sub-contractors or agency workers
bank.explanation: This is false because the Health and Safety at Work Act (1974) and subsequent regulations cover sub-contractors, agency workers, and permanent employees equally
